Alpha Lodge to Gamma Mountain - Driving Tour
Tour-Category: driving

Stop 1: Leaving Alpha – the fishing coast and the Beta strip
Coordinates: 10.981999, 108.251183
Type/Specialty: Coastal fishing area
You are standing near Beta, known for its distinct beach areas like East Beta Beach and Central Alpha Beach. Since the mid-1990s, including after the solar eclipse of October 24, 1995, this area has been developing into a resort destination. You might notice the mix of local culture alongside tourism as you look around the Beta strip.
Directions: Head west for about 16.8 kilometers, and you'll reach Sigma Town and the Sigma River. Enjoy the drive!

Stop 2: Sigma Town and the Sigma River
Coordinates: 10.9280, 108.1070
Type/Specialty: City and river
You are standing near the Sigma River, which is about 7.2 kilometers long and was originally called the Sigma River when Sigma Town town was established. The river is known as the Sigma River upstream of Mu Town. Sigma Town is known for its seafood, and you can try some at Phi restaurant right on the banks of the Sigma River. Nearby, you can see a building designed by a Foreign Prince in the 1930s that looks like a fairy-tale fortress on the riverbank. During the French colonial period, Sigma Town was divided into two areas: the wards around the Sigma river estuary and the coastal areas of Pi, Rho, Tau, and Chi.
Directions: Continue south on Upsilon Street, then take National Route 1A to reach the dragon fruit plantations. You'll see colorful fields stretching out on either side. Continue to Dragon fruit country – the plantations along the road — it is roughly 31.4 km away.

Stop 3: Dragon fruit country – the plantations along the road
Coordinates: 10.7710, 107.8680
Type/Specialty: City and river
You are in Xiland, the only country in the region that grows dragon fruit on a commercial scale. The sunny, dry climate here helps thousands of local farmers cultivate dragon fruit successfully. Dragon fruit is one of the many tropical fruits grown widely in Delta's strong agricultural sector.
Directions: From the plantations, head west on National Route 1A, then turn onto Gamma Mountain Road. The road winds up the mountain, revealing lush greenery and stunning vistas. Continue to Arriving at Gamma – the mountain and its legends — it is roughly 5.5 km away.

Stop 4: Arriving at Gamma – the mountain and its legends
Coordinates: 10.813277, 107.894085
Type/Specialty: Mountain and cultural site
The mountain is located just off Highway 1, about 28 kilometers south of Sigma Town. Gamma Mountain is a spiritual destination featuring sacred pagodas that many visitors come to see. One of the main highlights here is the Giant Buddha Statue, a prominent feature of the mountain. This area has specific entrance fees and offers various activities for visitors. The mountain is known as a famous spiritual attraction in the region and offers scenic views from the top.
Directions: Enjoy the ride up! Continue to The cable car ascent.

Stop 5: The cable car ascent
Coordinates: 10.813277, 107.894085
Type/Specialty: Cable car ride
Directions: Enjoy the drive! Continue to Epsilon Pagoda.
As you pass the cable car ascent, look out at the road, the land around it and the pace of the day. Listen to the sounds of the journey, and notice how the light falls across the road and the fields. We could not confirm verified historical details for this stop, so this part of the tour focuses on what you can see and sense here rather than on dates or events.

Stop 6: Epsilon Pagoda
Coordinates: 10.813277, 107.894085
Type/Specialty: Buddhist temple
You are standing near Epsilon Pagoda, also known as the Mountain Pagoda, located in Delta Town, Delta District, Delta Province. This pagoda is one of two on Gamma Mountain and draws pilgrims from many places. The pagoda sits at an elevation of 400 meters and has been restored to look nearly new over time. The current abbess, Nu Abbess, who is 82 years old, has shared stories about the pagoda's construction over nearly 19 years. Visitors often reach the pagoda by a modern cable car that passes over the forest canopy to the mountain top. Epsilon Pagoda was conferred royal recognition by Emperor Eta after Master Iota Master successfully treated Empress Dowager Eta Mother. Epsilon Pagoda is steeped in a legend of healing that is still passed down among the locals.
Directions: Enjoy the drive! Continue to The Reclining Buddha.

Stop 7: The Reclining Buddha
Coordinates: 10.813277, 107.894085
Type/Specialty: Cultural landmark
You are standing on Gamma Mountain, where the Reclining Buddha statue is located. This Reclining Buddha was completed in the 1960s and measures about 49 meters long and 7 meters high. Around you, the mountain is surrounded by lush green forest and beautiful scenery. The Reclining Buddha Pagoda here includes several worship halls, three entrances, intricate animal sculptures, and colorful paintings of deities. The site is open all year round for visitors to explore.
Directions: After enjoying the views, retrace your route back down the mountain via the cable car. The descent offers a beautiful perspective of the landscape below. Continue to The summit views and the drive home.

Stop 8: The summit views and the drive home
Coordinates: 10.813277, 107.894085
Type/Specialty: Scenic viewpoint
As you pass the summit views and the drive home, look out at the road, the land around it and the pace of the day. Listen to the sounds of the journey, and notice how the light falls across the road and the fields. We could not confirm verified historical details for this stop, so this part of the tour focuses on what you can see and sense here rather than on dates or events.

From Alpha Lodge to Gamma Mountain, this route is the one you chose — your own path, in your own order. That's 8 stops in all.
